summary: Facepalm: Thin day for facepalm stories. One candidate found: Fountain Hills, Ariz., council bans license plate readers the town doesn't have. Other leads were out of the window, lacked a second accepted source, or involved mental-health or animal-only stories. Genius: No genius candidate cleared the rules this run. Searches covered science, medicine, space, prizes, sports and student feats. Results were mostly reposts, items outside the window or outside the U.S., or leads with no accepted second source. Two stories are already on the bench: the Voyager 1 light-day milestone and the National Book Award for fiction. No facepalm story met the standard; nothing published.

candidates.headline: Hannah Lillith Assadi's 'Paradiso 17' wins the 2026 National Book Award for fiction in New York
Fountain Hills, Arizona, council bans license plate readers the town does not have
candidates.reason: It isn't absurd on its face. Both sources describe a forward-looking policy ordinance, not a council banning something that doesn't exist. License plate readers exist. The town's police contractor, the Maricopa County Sheriff's Office, presented to the council, said it wanted the cameras as a tool and estimated it could use about four at the town's entrances and exits (ABC15). The ban stops that from happening, which is the point of the ordinance.; The headline and summary leave out that context, so the vote looks pointless. That makes the facepalm framing misleading by omission.; Calling this a facepalm takes a side in a live policy debate, privacy versus policing, after Flock camera misuse cases led several Arizona cities to cancel their contracts (azfamily). A fair reader who supports the ban would see it as a sneer at a legitimate policy choice. The rules say politicians and officials are fair game for what they did, never for their views, and this is at least arguably about a view. Under the rules, an arguable case means reject.; Minor point: the sources spell the drafting councilman's name differently ('Alan' in ABC15, 'Allen' in azfamily). The summary doesn't name him, so this doesn't affect the copy.
